title: The eight Legions
summary: How Stygia sorts the Western dead.

claims.text: Stygia's eight Legions in theory hold every soul of the Western dead, each under a Deathlord, and they have been the powers of Stygia since Charon disappeared.
The Legions have military and civilian sides that together keep Stygia running; if they fail, Oblivion is waiting.
Stygians picture the Silent Legion's soldiers as wild Warriors of Lethe charging into Maelstroms, but the Legion is among the smallest and cannot spare troops for suicide charges.
The Quiet Lord only grudgingly tolerates the Warriors of Lethe as an exception.

title: Daredevils of the Emerald Legion
summary: Who ends up among the victims of chance.

claims.text: Extreme athletes make up a small, visible part of the Emerald Legion: skaters turn the Shadowlands into skate parks, BASE jumpers leap from Underworld landmarks with relic parachutes, and climbers scale Stygian towers.
Large groups of recruits arrive together after earthquakes, hurricanes, crashes, shipwrecks and explosions, so the Legion mostly holds no grudge against any living foe.

title: Freaks and misfits of the Paupers

claims.text: The Beggar Lord is known for taking in odd souls, on the view that useful wretches are better registered as Paupers than drifting into heresy or rebellion.
Such souls tend to grasp reality poorly and resist their Shadows weakly.

title: Legion units
summary: How the Legions organize their soldiers.

claims.text: Cohorts are the smallest units sent out alone, mostly on patrols and Spectre hunts; four to six cohorts form a company of 80 to 100 wraiths.

Companies handle long patrols, attacks on Renegade and Heretic strongholds and counterattacks on Spectres; each is led by a Regent who answers to the Provincial Overlord of Military Affairs, and most Provinces have one to three.
